correctness.rationale: From the published recurrence, q=i gives [x]_i=sin(pi x/2), a_0=cos(pi s/2), and a_1=sin(pi s/2). The j=0 equation gives u_1=a_0/g. The j=1 equation loses its u_2 term because [2]_i=0 and therefore requires g^2 sin(pi s)=a_0a_1=sin(pi s)/2. Under sin(pi s) nonzero this is exactly g^2=1/2; at equality u_2 is not determined by that equation. The explicit example s=i log(3)/pi, gamma=2, g=1 satisfies the representation relation and violates compatibility.

value.rationale: The free-fermion point is a standard XXZ regime, and rational anisotropies are known to have special auxiliary-space behavior. The exact compatibility condition identifies when a widely stated generic recurrence cannot be advanced from u_0=1 without additional treatment. This is a concrete, motivated boundary case; it does not overclaim nonexistence of a steady state.
